1. Review the whole pack using parallel helpers, one per source folder (sources/companies, sources/financials, sources/diligence-calls, sources/market). Each helper returns the figures it found with [src:<path>#L<line>] citations plus any superseded documents, diligence-call exceptions and references to restricted documents. Treat sources/restricted/ as unavailable and do not try to read it.
2. Build analysis/comparison.json (schema in analysis/README.md and report/src/table.mjs) and analysis/comparison.md with one row per company: ARR (restated where a diligence call restates it), YoY ARR growth, gross margin, average monthly net burn, cash, runway months = cash / monthly burn (one decimal), and the top risk from the company's diligence call. 5. Create a reusable skill named citation-validation with draft_skill, then validate_skill, test_skill and activate_skill. It must contain a Node script that takes a markdown file path as its first argument, resolves citation paths against the current working directory (the workspace root), and exits 0 only when every [src:...] citation resolves to an existing line that contains the number written before it, non-zero otherwise. Give it at least one passing example and one failing counterexample as test cases. Test cases run under Node's permission model and can read only the draft folder and the files passed as arguments, so keep the examples self-contained inside the draft (for example a --root=<dir> option and a small example source file in the draft). After activation, run the skill on analysis/comparison.md and fix anything it reports.
6. Finish with a short summary that names the restated company, the superseded document and the unavailable restricted documents, and states which checks passed.
